fusion_ranking.name: qkv_projection_block
fusion_ranking.pattern: per layer: k_proj.qmm, v_proj.qmm, q_proj.qmm (same lhs = input_layernorm output) + 3 bias adds -> 1 dispatch

sub_steps.step: bias add into qmm epilogue (qmm -> add(bias[N]) peephole)
sub_steps.exactness: bit-exact if the epilogue rounds the float accumulator to f16 first and then adds the f16 bias in float and rounds again (that is exactly what ElementwiseF16 op0 computes today)

sub_steps.step: shared-lhs multi-weight qmm (3 weight/scale/bias sets, one dispatch, column ranges routed by workgroup id)
sub_steps.exactness: bit-exact only if the fused kernel keeps qmm_vec.comp's per-column lane split and subgroup reduction order; then each output column is the same float dot product and only the dispatch grouping changes

fusion_ranking.kernel_work: new qmm_vec variant: bias binding + up to 3 weight sets (binding budget: 3x(w,scales,biases)+x+bias+out = 14 bindings; check binding_limit)

fusion_ranking.name: mlp_block
fusion_ranking.pattern: per layer: gate_proj.qmm, up_proj.qmm (same lhs), sigmoid, multiply, multiply -> 1 dispatch (dual-weight qmm with swiglu epilogue)

sub_steps.step: swiglu elementwise chain sigmoid(g) -> g*s -> (g*s)*u as one ElementwiseF16 chain kernel (MLX_OMARCHY_FUSED_CHAIN territory; 4864 elements, 3 ops)
sub_steps.exactness: bit-exact if each intermediate is rounded to f16 between ops exactly as the three separate kernels do

sub_steps.step: swiglu in the dual-qmm epilogue (lane owns gate[j] and up[j])
sub_steps.exactness: bit-exact with f16 rounding of gate, up, sigmoid, product, product in that order

fusion_ranking.kernel_work: qmm_vec dual-weight variant with epilogue; or fused_chain elementwise for the 3-op tail only

fusion_ranking.name: sdpa_vector
fusion_ranking.pattern: per layer: MatmulF16 (q@k^T, scale in alpha), SoftmaxF16, MatmulF16 (probs@v) -> 1 vector-SDPA dispatch (upstream Metal sdpa_vector does exactly this for q_len<=8)
fusion_ranking.exactness: NOT automatically bit-exact: today scores and probs are stored f16 between kernels; a fused kernel must round scores to f16 after the scaled dot, run softmax in float over those f16 scores, round probs to f16, then accumulate probs@v in float and round once - replicate that rounding sequence to keep token IDs identical
fusion_ranking.kernel_work: new sdpa_vector.comp: one workgroup per (kv_head, repeat) query row, loops over k_len (53 here) - also removes the 5-D regroup view temporaries

fusion_ranking.name: residual_add_plus_rms_norm
fusion_ranking.pattern: per layer x2: residual add (h = x + r) immediately followed by mx.fast.rms_norm(h) on the same 896-vector -> 1 dispatch with two outputs (h and norm(h)); pairs: residual_add_attn+post_attention_layernorm, residual_add_mlp+next layer input_layernorm (layer 23 pairs with model.norm)
fusion_ranking.exactness: bit-exact: write h rounded to f16 exactly as ElementwiseF16 op0 does, then run the existing rms_norm math on that f16 h in the same workgroup
fusion_ranking.kernel_work: fast_rms_norm variant with an optional residual operand and second output; the residual output must still be materialized because the next residual add reads it

fusion_ranking.name: cache_write_redirect
fusion_ranking.pattern: per layer x2: rope(keys) -> CopyGeneralF16 slice_update into cache.keys; v_proj.bias_add -> CopyGeneralF16 slice_update into cache.values. The producer can write straight into the (donated, in-place) cache slot with an output offset/stride, deleting the copy
fusion_ranking.kernel_work: graph peephole: producer output consumed only by an in-place SliceUpdate -> hand the producer the destination binding + offset; FastRope and ElementwiseF16 already take output offsets/strides in ComputeParams

fusion_ranking.name: rope_q_and_k_one_dispatch
fusion_ranking.pattern: per layer: FastRopeF16 (queries, 14 heads) and FastRopeF16 (keys, 2 heads) share offset/base/scale -> one dispatch over 16 head rows
fusion_ranking.kernel_work: two-segment rope dispatch (second input/output binding pair)

fusion_ranking.name: embedding_gather_dequant
fusion_ranking.pattern: per token: 3 Take + DequantF16 -> 1 gather-dequant dispatch
fusion_ranking.kernel_work: small: dequant kernel that indexes rows

fusion_ranking.name: logprob_tail
fusion_ranking.pattern: per token: LogSumExpF16 + subtract + ArgReduceF16 -> 1 or 2 dispatches (argmax of logits equals argmax of logits-lse; the subtract output is only used for returned logprobs)
fusion_ranking.exactness: argmax bit-exact; logprobs array still needed by mlx-lm generate_step return value, so keep the subtract unless mlx-lm is changed

gap_model.reading: busy + intra + inter (~54 ms) reproduces the instrumented inter-token interval (~54 ms) to within 1%, so the instrumented GPU timeline is closed: nothing else is hiding. But the uninstrumented token is 14.2 ms, so ~40 ms/token of the instrumented gaps is timestamp/drain artifact. The profile cannot decompose the real 14.2 ms into floor vs work; only the dispatch ORDER and COUNTS, and the RELATIVE gap structure below, transfer.

qmm_vec_gap_vs_bound_weight_bytes.fit: gap_before_us = 29.9 + 101.0 * weight_MB (least squares over 4200 QmmVecSubgroupF16 dispatches, tokens 5-29)

gap_model.answer_to_parent: No: QmmVecSubgroupF16 gaps are NOT the same ~22 us floor as tiny elementwise kernels. The floor for ElementwiseF16/FastRope/CopyGeneral/Softmax is p50 20-23 us. Before a QmmVec the gap scales linearly with the bound weight buffer: 57 KB (k/v_proj) 35 us, 401 KB (q/o_proj) 62 us, 2.18 MB (gate/up/down) 243 us, 68 MB (lm_head) 6905 us = 29.9 us + 101 us/MB, i.e. ~10 GB/s over the weight bytes. Group count does not explain it (down_proj 112 groups and gate_proj 608 groups both sit at ~243 us; q_proj 112 groups sits at 62 us). Per token that size term is 24*(3*0.22+2*0.04+2*0.006)+6.9 = 25.6 ms, which is MORE than the whole uninstrumented token (14.2 ms), so at least most of it is an artifact of the per-dispatch BOTTOM_OF_PIPE timestamp pair (a drain/flush whose recovery cost tracks the next kernel's footprint - TLB/page-table or cache refill at ~10 GB/s = ~1.6 us per 16 KB page). Two things follow. (1) Fusion count IS the lever for the flat part: every dispatch pays the same ~22 us instrumented floor regardless of size, and 585 of them is the count to cut. (2) The real uninstrumented budget is 14.2 ms for 247 MB of 4-bit weights per token (24 x 7.45 MB + 68 MB lm_head) = at least 17 GB/s effective weight streaming already; macOS 6.6 ms needs >= 37 GB/s. So after the dispatch count is cut, qmm_vec weight-streaming efficiency is the second lever, and the QmmVec durations in this profile (p50 12-15 us for 2.18 MB = 145 GB/s, above M1 DRAM bandwidth) prove the weight read is NOT inside the measured kernel span - it lands in the pre-dispatch gap. Decisive uninstrumented test (needs a jwm1 grant): submit 100 back-to-back QmmVecSubgroupF16 dispatches on the 68 MB lm_head weights in one command buffer with no timestamps and time the join. ~690 ms means the 10 GB/s weight stream is real and the qmm kernel/bandwidth is the primary lever; ~5-20 ms means it is a profiler artifact and dispatch count is the only lever.
